Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM
is seeking an Environmental Scientist II
to join our Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) team. We are seeking candidates to fill a seconded role as an on-site Health & Safety Specialist for a program in Rancho Cordova, California
. This full-time position within our Environmental group will provide and coordinate support related to Health & Safety and Environmental Compliance in a research and development laboratory and office setting. The duration of this position will be contingent upon AECOM maintaining our contract with the client.

Job Summary/Responsibilities:

Manage and support health, safety and environmental projects and programs, including planning, coordination, execution, and tracking of deliverables to ensure compliance and timely completion.
Conduct on‑site inspections to evaluate compliance with federal, state, and local environmental regulations (e.g., air, water, waste, hazardous materials).
Review permits, plans, records, and monitoring data to verify adherence to regulatory requirements and permit conditions.
Identify violations, non‑conformances, and environmental risks; document findings through clear, detailed inspection reports.
Investigate citizen complaints, spill reports, or alleged violations and determine appropriate enforcement or corrective actions.
Communicate findings and compliance requirements to facility representatives; provide technical guidance on corrective measures and best practices.
Coordinate with regulatory agencies and internal stakeholders to support enforcement actions, follow‑up inspections, or compliance reviews.
Maintain inspection records, databases, and tracking systems to ensure accurate documentation and timely reporting.
Interpret and apply relevant regulations (e.g., Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, RCRA, EPCRA) to inspection activities and compliance determinations.
Participate in compliance assistance outreach, training sessions, or stakeholder meetings to promote environmental stewardship and regulatory awareness.
Interprets and records data, conducts analyses, compares findings to relevant studies and local, state and federal regulations to ensure compliance. Work is performed with minimal direction.
Performing complex assignments often requires the development of unique solutions to problems.
Participating in internal and client required calls.

About AECOM’s Environment Business Line

Join AECOM to be part of an expert global team who is connected through a well-developed, worldwide, internal technical practice network through which you can learn from and brainstorm with the best in the world. AECOM is an industry-leading, world class environmental firm, and we want you to succeed within it. We respect and encourage your own pathway to excellence via our Freedom to Grow initiative.

AECOM is known for our award-winning technical excellence, leading-edge science and innovative project delivery. We provide sustainable solutions for some of the world’s most challenging issues. Our global clients and their projects span a variety of market sectors and geographies and require innovative technical solutions to solve wide-ranging environmental problems.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements:

BA/BS in related sciences.
2 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education in supporting environmental projects related to health and safety and environmental compliance.
Valid U.S. Driver's license is required for this role.
Due to the nature of work, US citizenship is required.
Candidate must be able to meet medical clearance requirements of an OSHA (HAZWOPER) medical surveillance physical exam.

Preferred Qualification

4+ years of relevant experience working on environmental projects related to health and safety and environmental compliance in California.
Previous experience with research and development laboratories.
Previous experience working as an environmental consultant.
OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER Training with annual 8-hour refresher.

Additional Information

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $74000 to $88000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Hawkesbury City Council is the largest local government area in metropolitan NSW covering 2,800 square kilometres, incorporating both urban and rural communities. We are committed to working together to deliver outcomes for the community through innovation and best practice.

Hawkesbury City Council strives to be an inclusive workplace for all people. We welcome and encourage applications from all ages and genders, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people from culturally diverse backgrounds, the LGBTIQ+ community, veterans and people with disabilities.

The Role

Responsibilities

Reporting to the Environmental Compliance Coordinator and based in Windsor, the successful candidate will join a high-performing team committed to continuous improvement. The position is responsible for:

Investigating environmental, public health and pollution complaints.
Delivering the annual public health inspection programs.
Assessing development applications from an environmental health perspective.
Working collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders to protect community health and the environment.
Contributing to ongoing service improvements and regulatory outcomes

About You

You have demonstrated experience in Environmental Health within local government and public health settings, with a proven ability to manage complex regulatory issues and deliver balanced, practical outcomes. We are currently seeking an experienced Environment Specialist to join the Asset Retirement HSE team of a leading global oil & gas organisation.

The Environment Specialist will provide practical environmental guidance and assurance across field-based operations and projects, with a strong focus on environmental compliance, risk management and continuous improvement.

Key responsibilities will include:

Conducting field-based environmental assurance, verification and validation activities across Asset Retirement worksites.
Supporting environmental monitoring and sampling programs covering air, water, waste and soil.

Supporting environmental risk assessments and the implementation of appropriate controls.

A Diploma or Degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Management or a related discipline.

We provide advisory and technical services to ensure compliance, manage impacts, and reduce risks, including obtaining permits and approvals, decommissioning and restoring contaminated sites, and tackling climate change challenges and resilience. We focus on preserving habitats, water quality, stakeholder engagement and cultural resources, promoting a holistic approach to environmental impact management at every project stage.

**Everyone belongs at AECOM**


We’re committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging \- because great ideas come from diverse perspectives. AECOM is proud to be a Fortune 500 Most Admired Company , a WGEA Employer of Choice for Gender Equality , \# Work180 Equitable Workplace Awards 2025 Winner and an AWEI Bronze Tier LGBTQ\+ Inclusive Employer .

**How you’ll make a difference**

* Delivery of air quality impact assessments, monitoring and management programs and related technical studies, ensuring high technical standards and timely delivery.
* Manage air quality projects from initiation to completion as part of a team of air quality professionals, including client engagement, reporting and proposal development.
* Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams across AECOM’s business lines, including a strong national and international Air Quality practice.
* Contribute to greenhouse gas and carbon accounting projects
* Supporting business development activities for the Air Quality practice along with technical profile raising activities to grow personal capabilities.

  

**Qualifications** **The qualities that help you thrive**


The following qualifications and experience are highly desired, but if you don’t tick all the boxes you could still be a perfect fit for this role. Please apply, all applications will be considered.

* Bachelor’s degree in Science, Engineering, Environmental Management or a related discipline with 2\+ years’ experience in air quality or environmental consulting.
* Proficiency in air quality dispersion modelling (e.g. CALPUFF, AERMOD) with experience in GRAL or WRF viewed favourably.
* Experience developing emission inventories, including the use of excel for emissions estimation calculations.
* Strong technical writing and communication skills, with experience preparing reports (e.g. Air Quality Impact Assessments, Air Quality Management Plans), proposals and engaging directly with clients.
* Familiarity with greenhouse gas or carbon accounting and air quality monitoring.
* Abilities in GIS (e.g. ArcGIS Pro, Q\-GIS) and programming (e.g. R, Python) would be viewed favourably.

Committed to our core principles in health and safety, and environment and sustainability.

Between 8-12+ years of experience in a similar role across consulting services in Australia.

Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal – particularly across report writing and computer literacy.
Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to work efficiently in teams.

Full and unrestricted working rights in Australia.

We are proud of our One Team culture where we work together to collaborate on projects to get the best possible outcome for our clients and team. We recognise that every person is different, and our benefits aim to ensure that we cater for all.

Be part of an organisation that is Making Sustainability Happen – apply now.

**What if you could do the kind of work the world needs?**

At WSP, you can access our global scale, contribute to landmark projects and connect with the brightest minds in your field to do the best work of your life. You can embrace your curiosity in a culture that celebrates new ideas and diverse perspectives. You can experience a world of opportunity and the chance to shape a career as unique as you

* Leading contaminated land investigations, including soil, groundwater and vapour assessments.
* Providing technical leadership, review and advice across complex contaminated land and remediation projects.
* Managing project performance, including budgets, schedules, resources and risk.
* Developing and maintaining strong client relationships while acting as a trusted advisor.
* Preparing and reviewing technical reports and recommendations in accordance with relevant legislation, standards and guidelines.
* Leading and supporting remediation planning and implementation activities.
* Mentoring and developing junior team members while promoting a strong safety and quality culture.
Supporting business development activities, including proposals, pursuits and identifying opportunities to grow client relationships.

We're seeking a respected contaminated land professional with strong technical capability, leadership experience and a passion for developing people and delivering exceptional client outcomes.

* Bachelor's degree in Earth Sciences, Environmental Engineering or equivalent.
* At least 7 years' experience in contaminated land assessment, remediation and environmental consulting.
* Strong understanding of NSW contaminated land legislation, frameworks and regulatory processes.
* Proven experience managing project risk, budgets, schedules and delivery on substantial projects.
* Demonstrated ability to prepare and review high\-quality technical reports and provide practical client\-focused advice.
* Experience developing and maintaining strong client relationships.
* Proven capability supervising, mentoring and developing environmental professionals and field teams.
* Strong communication skills with the ability to guide clients through regulatory processes and complex technical challenges.
Commitment to safety, quality and technical excellence.  
* 

**Why WSP?**

At WSP, we value our people and our reputation. We are locally dedicated with international scale, future\-focused, collaborative and empowering — and we’re looking for people who share those values.


You’ll be part of a team that delivers technical excellence while keeping client outcomes, sustainability, quality and safety at the centre of what we do. You’ll also have the opportunity to grow your leadership capability, contribute to meaningful projects and help shape better outcomes for communities and clients.


Imagine a better future for you and a better future for us all.


Join our close\-knit community of talented individuals who share your passion for making a positive impact.


**With us, you can. Apply today.**

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist/Project Manager
jobs.description:
Do you like working with different project teams in a fast\-paced environment? Are you interested in joining an organization focused on making a positive impact? If so, we'd like to talk with you about growing with us.


EnSafe is seeking a full\-time Environmental Scientist/Project Manager to join our team of professionals at our San Diego, CA, office.



This position has a requirement to work onsite, at the office, if needed relocation assistance may be offered to meet this expectation.


**What we are looking for**



An Environmental Scientist with proven experience managing environmental due diligence projects and a strong ability to translate complex findings into clear, defensible Phase I ESA reports. You'll work with clients across California and beyond, managing projects from site assessment through final reporting while gaining exposure to Phase II investigations, environmental sampling, and emerging areas such as PFAS risk evaluation.



Joining our team means immersing yourself in an environment that nurtures creativity, encourages collaboration at all levels, fosters a supportive culture, and facilitates professional development.


***Key responsibilities of this position include***


***What you will be doing:***


* Perform and manage Phase I Environmental Site Assessments in accordance with ASTM and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Conduct site reconnaissance, historical research, regulatory database review, interviews, and other due diligence activities.
* Prepare clear, technically sound Phase I ESA reports and recommendations.
* Manage multiple Phase I ESA projects, including scope, schedule, budget, subcontractors, client communication, and deliverables.
* Provide technical and peer review of Phase I ESA reports as experience permits.
* Support Phase II environmental site investigations and other due diligence activities when warranted.
* Plan and conduct environmental sampling activities involving soil, groundwater, soil vapor, indoor air, surface water, or other environmental media.
* Prepare work plans, technical memoranda, investigation reports, and proposals.
* Communicate findings and environmental risk considerations clearly to clients and project teams.
* Coordinate work with junior staff and provide technical guidance and mentoring.
* Support environmental compliance projects based on experience and workload, which may include hazardous materials and hazardous waste management, SPCC, stormwater, wastewater, EPCRA/Tier II, or related regulatory requirements.
* Participate in business development activities, including preparation of scopes, budgets, proposals, and support for existing client relationships.
* Travel periodically to project sites throughout California and as needed, elsewhere in the United States.


***Minimum Skills and Requirements***


* Bachelor's degree in environmental science, Geology, Environmental Engineering, or a related scientific or engineering discipline.
* Approximately 6 or more years of relevant environmental consulting experience.
* Demonstrated experience preparing Phase I Environmental Site Assessments.
* Strong technical writing and report preparation skills.
* Ability to independently conduct site reconnaissance and evaluate environmental conditions.
* Working knowledge of environmental due diligence practices and applicable federal and state environmental regulations.
* Ability to manage schedules, budgets, client expectations, and multiple concurrent assignments.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong critical\-thinking and problem\-solving skills.
* Ability and willingness to travel to support project work.
* Valid driver's license and ability to perform field activities associated with environmental site assessments.


***Preferred Qualifications***


***The following experience would be beneficial but is not required:***


* Experience managing Phase I ESA programs or providing technical/peer review.
* Qualification as an Environmental Professional under ASTM/AAI requirements.
* Phase II ESA, subsurface investigation, soil, groundwater, or vapor assessment experience.
* Environmental compliance experience, including hazardous waste, hazardous materials, SPCC, stormwater, wastewater, CERS/HMBP, or EPCRA/Tier II reporting.
* Experience supporting industrial, commercial real estate, logistics/warehouse, energy, municipal, or similar clients.
* Professional Geologist (PG), Professional Engineer (PE), or other relevant professional certification.
* Building sciences or hazardous building materials experience.
* Experience with asbestos\-containing materials, lead\-based paint, mold/microbial assessments, or related building surveys.
* California asbestos or lead certifications.
* 40\-hour HAZWOPER training.


**Why Join EnSafe?**


* **Employee\-Owned Advantage**  

EnSafe is 100% employee\-owned, with an ESOP (Employee Stock Ownership Plan) since 1997\. That means when EnSafe succeeds, you succeed too, turning company growth directly into shared rewards.
* **Commitment to Growth and Wellness**  

The company supports personalized career development, mentorship, and employee wellness initiatives such as health tracking tools.
* **Purpose‑Driven Work**  

EnSafe's mission focuses on impactful environmental, health, and safety consulting—making a real difference in communities and is backed by its long\-standing technical credibility.
* **Safety as a Value, Not Just a Service**  

Safety is deeply embedded in our culture, prioritizing employee well\-being in addition to helping clients maintain compliance. We stress that *"safety is part of everything we do."*
* **A Culture of Freedom \& Ownership**  

At EnSafe, our career philosophy is built on freedom. The freedom to take initiative, achieve your goals, and shape your own career path Employees are encouraged to pursue growth in a flexible, entrepreneurial environment.
* **Challenging, Creative Work**  

Workdays at EnSafe are anything but ordinary,

Job Description And Duties

The Enforcement Division’s (ED) Engine and Parts Enforcement Section (EPES) is seeking a highly qualified and motivated Air Pollution Specialist (APS). EPES is responsible for enforcing California Air Resources Board (CARB) regulations designed to improve air quality by reducing emissions generated by (1) non-compliant engines, including large-spark ignition (LSI) engines and fleets, compression ignition (CI) engines, and small off-road engines (SOREs – engines rated less than 25 horsepower), (2) non-compliant aftermarket parts, including catalytic converters, fuel injectors, turbo chargers, superchargers, computer devices, sensors, and other engine performance enhancers, and (3) non-compliant portable fuel containers, marine fuel tanks, and refrigerant canisters. EPES is also responsible for the Laboratory and Certification Fraud Program.

Enforcement services provided by EPES focus primarily on investigating complaints, tips, and leads concerning potentially non- compliant engines, parts, specialty products, laboratory and certification fraud, initiating enforcement actions where violations are found, and resolving these cases, including providing support in cases that are referred for litigation.

This incumbent will investigate complaints, tips, and leads received from the public, industry, or affected stakeholders. In addition to laboratory and certification fraud, CARB has developed, mandated, implemented, and is invested in being the worldwide leader in On-Board Diagnostics (OBD) regulations to protect California's air quality. CARB's OBD Branch certifies manufacturer OBD systems in accordance with California regulatory requirements not only for California, but also for the United States, as EPA accepts, and at times, requires California OBD certification. Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world's leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we're keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Program Overview

Provide critical communications and tracking for multiple spacecraft from three complexes located globally, and operates year round 24 hours/7days to provide continuous contact with the spacecraft. The program fulfills NASA goals by supporting NASA deep space mission set, including NASA-funded missions and collaborative international missions.

About The Role

We are looking for a Lead Safety & Environmental Analyst
to support our Deep Space Network (DSN) Operations and Maintenance O&M contract with the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) and NASA in Fort Irwin, CA.

What You'll Do:

As Lead Safety & Environmental Analyst, your primary responsibility is ensuring the safety of personnel working in and around complex antenna, mechanical, and electrical systems at a remote government facility. You will lead safety programs, investigate incidents, drive risk reduction, and maintain regulatory compliance across the full spectrum of EHS disciplines - with a clear emphasis on occupational safety first.

Core Safety Responsibilities:

Lead and continuously improve site safety programs, with emphasis on high-hazard work (electrical, elevated, confined space, heavy equipment)
Conduct and lead incident investigations; identify root causes and drive corrective actions to closure
Conduct hazard assessments, job safety analysis (JSAs), and Management of Change (MOC) reviews
Perform and lead EHS audits, field observations, and self-assessments; report findings to leadership
Lead or support emergency response planning and exercises
Analyze safety performance data (OSHA 300 logs, LTIR, frequency rates) and present trends to stakeholders

Training & Compliance:

Develop and deliver EHS training programs; certify trainers where applicable (OSHA 500/501)
Ensure compliance with federal and California regulations (OSHA, Cal/OSHA, EPA, Cal/EPA, NFPA, APCD)
Manage Air Quality and Water programs, including regulatory reporting and agency coordination
Prepare internal and external compliance reports, including data analysis and trend summaries

Collaboration & Communication:

Serve as the primary EHS point of contact for site management, trade personnel, and JPL/NASA stakeholders
Represent the program in discussions with regulatory agencies and community stakeholders
Provide guidance and mentorship to junior EHS staff

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

BS/BA + 8 years of experience; MS/MA + 6 years; PhD + 3 years; or 4 years of directly relevant experience in lieu of degree
Strong knowledge of OSHA, Cal/OSHA, EPA, NIOSH, NFPA, and APCD regulations; NASA familiarity is a plus
Demonstrated experience leading safety programs in complex industrial or government facility environments
Experience with construction safety oversight and managing shifting project priorities
Ability to analyze EHS data and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
Valid California driver's license (Read-ID)
U.S. citizenship required; must pass background check and NCIC screening

Preferred Qualifications:

Certified Safety Professional (CSP) or OHST/CHST (BCSP)
OSHA 500/501 Train-the-Trainer certification
Prior experience in government or DOD facility contracts

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
About Tower Semiconductor

Looking for a career path in the high-tech industry? Become part of a team focused on delivering the most exciting semiconductor technology in the world! If you enjoy working with others in a dynamic, fast-paced environment and are looking for an opportunity to grow your career in this exciting industry, then Tower Semiconductor is the place to be!

Tower Semiconductor, the leading foundry of high-value analog semiconductor solutions, provides technology, development, and process platforms for analog integrated circuits to more than 300 customers worldwide across growing markets such as communications, mobile, infrastructure, consumer, industrial, automotive, medical, and aerospace and defense, among others.

Join Tower and become part of a dynamic organization with exceptionally talented and dedicated team members who work collaboratively to provide best-in-class technological solutions to our clients.

Job Description

An Environmental Specialist is responsible for ensuring uninterrupted manufacturing operations through proactive environmental compliance, risk identification, regulatory engagement, and timely execution of critical Environmental programs. The role supports semiconductor manufacturing operations by ensuring compliance with environmental regulations governing air emissions, wastewater treatment, hazardous waste management, and chemical handling.

This position works closely with manufacturing, facilities, engineering, operations, and corporate EHS teams to minimize environmental risk, maintain regulatory compliance, and support safe and reliable fab operations.

This Job Is For You If

You can ensure compliance with federal, state, and local environmental regulations (e.g., 40 CFR, 30 TAC) related to air emissions, hazardous waste, wastewater, stormwater, and chemical management.
You can proactively identify compliance risks, operational vulnerabilities, and permitting gaps, and escalate issues early to management with clear mitigation plans.
You can maintain accurate environmental records, emissions inventories, permit tracking systems, and regulatory submissions to ensure timely and compliant reporting
You can oversee hazardous waste management, hazardous material shipping, and Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) programs.
You can manage air compliance programs including stack testing, Leak Detection and Repair (LDAR), greenhouse gas (GHG) monitoring, and criteria pollutant tracking.
You can monitor wastewater treatment systems and implement Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPP).
You can lead regulatory inspections and agency interactions with professionalism, technical competence, and strong preparation.
You can conduct facility audits and inspections of chemical storage, waste accumulation, and environmental control systems.
You can investigate environmental incidents, determine root causes, and drive timely corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs).
You can coordinate effectively across operations, facilities, engineering, production, and corporate EHS teams to ensure alignment and execution of environmental priorities.
You can develop and maintain environmental procedures, standards, and training programs to ensure ongoing compliance and operational readiness.
You can prepare and submit environmental reports including Toxic Release Inventory (TRI), Tier II, emissions inventories, and Discharge Monitoring Reports.
You can implement programs that minimize environmental risk, business interruption, and operational impact.
You can manage multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment while maintaining high accuracy, responsiveness, and attention to detail.

Job Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Occupational Safety and Health, or a related field required.
Minimum 5 years of environmental compliance experience, preferably within semiconductor manufacturing or other highly regulated industrial operations.
Extensive knowledge of environmental regulations, permitting requirements, and regulatory reporting.
Experience managing environmental compliance programs related to air, waste, water, and hazardous materials.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational, analytical, and project management skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and environmental tracking/reporting systems.
Ability to conduct inspections in manufacturing and industrial environments.
Must be able to lift and carry up to 25 pounds as needed.
Ability to sit, stand, walk, and work on a computer for extended periods as required by the role.

Preferred Characteristics

Strong sense of ownership and accountability
Proactive communicator with excellent follow-through
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities
Comfortable operating in high-visibility, high-responsibility environments
Strong cross-functional collaboration and coordination skills
High attention to detail and strong organizational discipline

Compensation: $106,000/year - $124,000/year

Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is currently initiating a search for an Early Career Environmental Scientist for our Portland, OR office. Be involved in projects with our Advisory & Planning Team and be a part of a growing organization that meets our clients’ objectives and solves their challenges.

Takes part in providing local technical assistance for the collection, identification, and compiling of observational and spatial data concerning a variety of biological, physical, and earth sciences. Provides local assistance for the development of processes and infrastructure relating to water supply, air emission, pollution control, cultural impact, and preserving the quality of the environment by identifying, controlling, and preventing disruption to environmental systems and species caused by human activity. Generates accurate and concise documentation, ensuring that responsibilities are delivered and adhered to with a level of quality that meets or exceeds acceptable industry standards.

Your Impact

Under general supervision, conduct natural resource field surveys collecting observational, spatial, and environmental data.
Under general supervision, collect and compile samples of air, soil, water, sludge, and other matrices for analysis.
Maintain quality control standards and procedures for accurate and precise measurement and documentation.
Assist with performing basic professional environmental science work relating to ecological systems, air, and water resources, assisting with verifying the characteristics of a site and providing entry-level technical assistance on various environmental issues.

jobs.title: Senior Sediment Remediation Specialist
jobs.description:
Responsibilities  

  

The Senior Sediment Remediation Specialist will lead complex environmental investigations and the design of cleanup strategies for contaminated sediment sites in riverine, lacustrine, estuarine, and marine environments. This senior role requires a seasoned professional to provide technical, managerial, regulatory, and business development support to LimnoTech’s existing contaminated sediments practice. Typical job responsibilities include the following, depending on individual ability, skills, and experience:  

* Leading and overseeing technical work for the full lifecycle of sediment projects, which may include developing site characterization, remedial investigation (RI), and feasibility study (FS) plans; overseeing multi\-media sampling programs (sediment, water, biota, etc.); data interpretation (geostatistics, fingerprinting, etc.); numerical modeling (hydrodynamic, contaminant fate and transport, etc.); developing conceptual site models; evaluating and implementing remedial alternatives (dredging, capping, MNR, etc.); remedial cost estimating; and translating complex scientific findings into high quality technical written/verbal deliverables. Litigation support and expert witness experience is desirable.
* Managing projects through the full project management life cycle, including developing scopes of work, managing budgets, leading and mentoring project teams, coordinating with multi\-disciplinary teams of scientist, engineers, regulators, and responsible parties, delivering high quality deliverables on time and on budget, and client management.
* Providing regulatory expertise on contaminated sediment projects (e.g.: CERCLA, RCRA, or local state programs), which may include agency negotiations.
* Leading and participating in marketing and business development activities, which may include tracking and pursuing relevant requests for proposals, developing marketing documents (quals packages, project profiles, web articles, etc.), cultivating and nurturing client and partner relationships, and actively participating at relevant conferences (e.g.: Battelle).
  

  

Qualifications  

  

The ideal candidate will possess a minimum of a Bachelor of Science degree in Civil or Environmental Engineering, Geology, Environmental Science, or a closely related physical science discipline with 10 or more years of experience in the field. A Master’s degree or Ph.D. is strongly preferred, as the role demands a deep understanding of complex contaminant transport, sediment geochronology, and geochemical partitioning.  

* For engineering applicants, an active Professional Engineer (PE) license is expected; for scientists, a Professional Geologist (PG) or related credentials would be highly valued, demonstrating a commitment to professional standards and the ability to seal technical documents.
* In addition to formal academic credentials, specialized training in hydrodynamic modeling or statistical data analysis is a significant advantage.
* Candidates must also have completed the 40\-hour OSHA HAZWOPER certification with current annual refreshers, ensuring they are qualified to oversee field activities at hazardous waste sites.
* Continuous education through participation in industry organizations, such as the Battelle Sediment Conference or ITRC technical teams, is encouraged to ensure the firm remains at the forefront of emerging remediation technologies and evolving regulatory frameworks.
* A demonstrated interest or experience in urban waterfront restoration, engineering with nature, or nature\-based solutions is a plus.
* Must be legally able to work in the U.S. for any employer (proper documentation is required).
  

  

Compensation  

  

Individual achievement is rewarded through a unique merit review process based on recommendations from colleagues at all levels of the company, plus positive feedback from clients. This system drives pay increases and opportunities for increased project and corporate responsibility. We track individual progress annually to ensure competitiveness within our industry and identify opportunities for targeted professional development. The salary for this position will be determined based on the candidate’s years and type of experience, degrees earned, office location, and fit with job requirements, and is expected to range between $110,000 and $200,000 annually.  

  

Our company culture focuses on giving our people opportunities to improve and grow through training, conferences, workshops, seminars, and participation in professional organizations. We also favor more personal, self\-directed career planning over traditional performance evaluations. We encourage a mix of mentoring and proactive self\-management so individuals can explore and create work opportunities that further their careers.

jobs.title: PFAS Program Manager
jobs.description:
Company Overview

EKI Environment & Water, Inc. (EKI) is an employee-owned environmental, water resources, and engineering consulting firm serving private- and public-sector clients throughout the United States. If you are interested in improving the environment and advancing your career, then EKI is the place for you.

The PFAS Program Manager reports to the Executive Vice President, ESG, and is responsible for coordinating and advancing EKI’s national PFAS practice. Working collaboratively with EKI’s PFAS technical experts, Regional Directors, Technical Directors, Principals, and Project Managers, the PFAS Program Manager will organize and integrate EKI’s PFAS capabilities, support high-quality project execution, identify and develop opportunities with existing and new client relationships, develop innovative service offerings, and help position EKI as a recognized leader in PFAS consulting.

The PFAS Program Manager will serve as a catalyst for collaboration across EKI’s PFAS practitioners and will help connect technical capabilities with client and market needs. The role combines technical project execution, practice development, internal coordination, client engagement, and business development. Success in the position will require strong technical judgement, the ability to work effectively with and leverage EKI’s subject-matter experts, and the leadership and initiative to build a coordinated and effective PFAS practice.

Principal Duties & Responsibilities

Your responsibilities may include, but will not be limited to the following:

Advance EKI's PFAS practice by bringing together PFAS practitioners across the company; fostering and promoting knowledge sharing; developing training programs; supporting recruitment of PFAS professionals; identifying technical capabilities, resource needs, and capability gaps; and helping establish priorities and initiatives for continued development of the practice.
Develop and expand PFAS opportunities with strategic clients by working with Regional Directors, Technical Directors, Practice Area Directors, Principals, Project Managers, and technical staff to identify PFAS needs and opportunities; developing client-specific strategies; and connecting EKI’s PFAS capabilities with client needs.
Lead strategic pursuits by developing capture strategies; preparing and presenting major proposals; supporting interviews; and collaborating across the company to secure high-value projects.
Work collaboratively with EKI's PFAS technical experts to strengthen and continuously improve technical standards, QA/QC protocols, workflows, best practices, and innovative approaches that promote technical excellence, consistency, and high-quality project delivery across the company.
Advance EKI's PFAS technical capabilities and competitive position by monitoring emerging regulations, research, analytical methods, and treatment technologies; identifying opportunities for innovation and new service offerings, and strategic partnerships; and recommending strategic investments in staff, technology, and capabilities.
Strengthen EKI’s external visibility and reputation in PFAS through client and regulatory engagement; technical publications and presentations; industry conferences, technical committees, and other external forums.
Serve in substantive technical and project leadership roles on PFAS projects by developing investigation and management strategies; evaluating data; developing technical approaches and recommendations; preparing and reviewing technical work products; and communicating findings and recommendations to clients and regulators.
Other duties as required.

Qualifications & Requirements

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or Environmental Engineering; Master’s degree preferred

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Minimum of eight (8) years of relevant environmental and PFAS consulting experience
Professional Engineer license in the State of California or be able to obtain license following employment
Demonstrated ability to develop business opportunities and expand services within the environmental consulting industry
Excellent client management skills with a proven ability to develop and maintain long-term client relationships
Proven track record managing complex environmental projects involving regulatory compliance and stakeholder coordination
Established relationships with regulatory agencies, industry organizations, and/or key industrial clients strongly preferred
Demonstrated professional engagement in the PFAS field through publications, conference presentations, regulatory engagement, industry organizations, or other professional activities
Proven project management experience, including leading multidisciplinary teams and managing project budgets, schedules, scope and quality to deliver complex project on time and within budget
Demonstrated ability to organize and lead collaborative initiatives across teams, offices, or technical disciplines, including the ability to influence and build alignment without direct supervisory authority

Competencies

Must have strong verbal and written communication skills, including experience preparing high-quality technical reports, proposals, and client deliverables, and the ability to communicate and coordinate effectively with clients, subconsultants, regulatory agencies, and members of the public
Must have ability to lead multiple project teams
Must have demonstrated time management skills, strong work ethic and attention to detail
Must have a demonstrated commitment to personal and professional growth, including the mentorship of others
Must have a current valid driver’s license

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT

Must be able to work in a fast-paced environment with high-volume workload and frequent short deadlines
Must have the ability to obtain medical clearance to work on hazardous waste site(s)
Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs
Must be able to work remaining in a stationary position, often standing or sitting for prolonged periods
Must be able to communicate with others to exchange information
Must be able to assess the accuracy, quality and thoroughness of the work assigned

jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Specialist
jobs.description:
Title: EHS Specialist

Locations: Mountain View, CA (Fully Onsite)

Duration: Contract (6+ Months - Extendable)

Client: Aviation & Aerospace domain

Job Description:

We are seeking EHS Specialists (Contractors) to join our team. The goal of this position is to support the hands-on deployment, execution, and monitoring of practical EHS programs, ensuring our day-to-day workplace operations actively embody our core cultural behavior: “Safety Is Our Cornerstone.” You will join the EHS team, working boots on the ground to maintain total regulatory compliance and evaluate hazard points across our fast-paced aerospace environments.
Due to the nature of the work required for this position, this is an onsite opportunity. You will be required to work from our Mountain View, CA office, with flexibility to support or travel to local remote facilities as required by operational needs.
In this role you will own the day-to-day practical execution of core environmental, health, and safety protocols across R&D, Engineering, laboratories, and advanced manufacturing spaces.
As a mid-level specialist, you will bridge the gap between high-level policy and real-world implementation by conducting routine field audits, managing chemical and hazardous waste inventories, and facilitating employee safety training. You will collaborate directly with engineers, technicians, and floor operators to perform Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs) and incident investigations and ensure proper risk mitigation is in place. You will be instrumental in fostering a transparent, "Just Culture" workspace that enables cutting-edge aerospace development to proceed safely.

What you will do:

You will provide critical boots on the ground EHS support for our Bay Area facilities, helping to deploy specialized EHS solutions tailored to advanced air taxi development.
You will manage and maintain daily ownership over core workplace safety programs including Injury and Illness Prevention Plans (IIPP), Hazard Communication, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), Machine Guarding, Respiratory Protection, Electrical Safety/NFPA 70e, and Powered Industrial Trucks.
You will support Engineering, Manufacturing, R&D, and Flight Test teams by conducting proactive Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs).

jobs.title: Air Quality Managing Consultant
jobs.description:
Job Description

Position Description

We are seeking an experienced air quality professional to provide technical leadership and project delivery support within Ramboll’s Air and Climate Service Line. This position will focus on complex air dispersion modelling, air quality impact assessment, client advisory services, project management, and mentoring of junior to mid-level colleagues.

The role offers an opportunity to contribute to a growing national air quality practice while working collaboratively across Australian and global teams. Candidates with experience in digital tools, data workflows, automation, GIS, or cross-region technical coordination will be well placed to support ongoing innovation in how air quality services are delivered.

Air Quality Managing Consultant

Working within the Air and Climate Service Line you will be responsible for identifying, conducting and developing air quality projects based on an understanding of business needs, challenges, opportunities and the marketplace. Ramboll is seeking an experienced Air Quality Modelling professional for this position. Our ideal candidate is a technical leader with a proven track record of managing complex, multi-faceted air quality modelling projects, mentoring junior staff, and serving as a trusted advisor to clients. You would be responsible for overseeing project staff and be responsible for project delivery across the air quality team.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Technical Leadership: Lead and deliver complex air quality dispersion modelling and environmental impact assessment projects using regulatory and specialist models such as AERMOD, CALPUFF, CALMET, GRAL/GRAMM, TAPM and WRF. Develop innovative approaches to solving complex air quality, odour, emissions inventory and post-processing challenges.
Project Management: Manage air quality projects, including scope, schedule, budget, resources and quality, to support on-time and on-budget delivery that meets client expectations. Supervise project teams and delegate tasks to junior staff as required.
Technical Review and Quality Assurance: Provide senior-level QA/QC review and technical oversight of modelling analyses, emissions inventories, impact assessments, management plans, approval inputs and technical reports prepared by project teams.
Client and Regulatory Engagement: Act as a trusted client advisor through the full project lifecycle, from early strategy and scoping through approvals, compliance and implementation. Lead or support technical discussions with regulators and approval authorities on behalf of clients.
Staff Mentoring and Development: Mentor junior to mid-level air quality staff by providing technical guidance, training, review and career development support.
Business Development: Contribute technical and business content to proposals, develop scopes of work, support strategic client engagement and identify opportunities for growth in air quality services.
Digital and Cross-Region Collaboration: Support efficient project delivery through digital and technical innovation coordinating with Australian, APAC and global colleagues where specialist input or shared capability is required.

You will be part of the Australian Air and Climate Service Line working within the Air Quality Team as a Managing Consultant. You will lead the delivery of air quality projects, providing technical leadership, project management, and mentoring to junior team members, while supporting the ongoing growth and development of Ramboll’s national air quality capability.

Reporting to the National Air and Climate Practice Lead, you will play a key role in strengthening Ramboll’s air quality services and contributing to the continued success of the team. The position offers the opportunity to collaborate with colleagues across Australia, APAC and our global network to enhance project delivery, provide specialist technical expertise, drive digital innovation and promote technical excellence across Ramboll’s national air quality team.

Qualifications

About You

From the moment you start we will support your personal and professional development so that you can continue to grow with the company. While we look forward to supporting your continued learning and development, for this role we have identified some qualifications, skills and capabilities that will set you up for success:

Bachelor or Post Graduate degree in Environmental Science, Chemistry, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering or related field with minimum 10 years of experience in air dispersion modelling and impact assessment.
Certified Air Quality Professional (CAQP) with the Clean Air Society of Australia and New Zealand and demonstrated involvement in profile raising activities (preferred).
Proficiency in meteorological and air dispersion modelling software such as AERMET, AERMOD, CALMET, CALPUFF, GRAMM, GRAL, TAPM and WRF.
Experience in development of air, odour and GHG emissions inventories across a wide range of industry sectors.
Strong technical knowledge and report writing skills, including preparation of Air Quality Impact Assessments, monitoring reports, Air Quality Management Plans and proposals.
Experienced project management skills, including direct client engagement. Business development skills are highly desirable, as is demonstrated experience in people management and/or mentoring.
Experience in ambient air quality monitoring, stack testing knowledge, climate risk assessment and/or noise monitoring and modelling, is not essential but would be highly regarded.
Experience in the following fields is highly desirable, including GIS software (e.g. ArcGIS Pro and Surfer), programming (e.g. R and Python), and analytical and data visualisation platforms (e.g. MS Power BI).
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to present complex technical, digital or data-related information clearly to clients, regulators and multidisciplinary project teams.

Additional Information

What we can offer you

Interesting and diverse projects
The opportunity to work with some of the best and brightest professionals in your field
Flexible work arrangements
Investment in your development
Leaders you can count on, guided by our Leadership Principles
Appreciation for the unique person you are
Inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects.

We recognise that some candidates only apply when they tick every box. However, passion and potential often outweigh a perfect resume and Ramboll’s supportive learning culture can help you grow. So, if this role resonates with you but you don't meet all the requirements, we encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect fit for this opportunity or another within our team.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll employs more than 18,000 people globally across 35 countries. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy, Management Consulting, and Architecture & Landscape. Combining local experience with global knowledge, we help shape the societies of tomorrow.

Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion are at the heart of what we do. At Ramboll, we believe that diversity is a strength and that different experiences and perspectives are essential to creating truly sustainable societies. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive work environment where everyone is able to flourish and reach their potential. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We invite applications from candidates of all backgrounds and characteristics. Please let us know if there are any changes, we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at job.advert.accessibility@ramboll.com with such requests.

jobs.title: Environmental Compliance Analyst
jobs.description:
About The Role

The City of Bend is accepting applications for one (1) regular, full-time Environmental Compliance Analyst in the Environmental Services Division of the Water Services Department. This is a COBEA represented, non-exempt (overtime-eligible) position. This position will be open until filled and may be used to create an eligibility list for future vacancies. Please review the entire job posting, including the application requirements at the end.

This role is all about helping the City understand what’s happening across its water systems, whether that’s drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, or local rivers and groundwater. On any given day, you might be out in the field collecting water samples, checking monitoring equipment, or downloading flow data from sites across the City. Other days may involve reviewing and validating that data, troubleshooting equipment issues, or helping respond to unusual conditions such as storm events. In simple terms, this position helps answer critical questions: Is our water safe? Are our systems functioning properly? Are we meeting environmental regulations?

This position offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of environmental science, public health, and infrastructure. Current and upcoming projects include expanding the City’s flow monitoring network and supporting the installation of new real-time level sensors that help detect and prevent system overflows. The role also contributes to groundwater and surface water monitoring, evolving regulatory compliance efforts, and improved data-driven decision-making.

This position plays a key support role across several City programs, including Industrial Pretreatment, Stormwater, Wastewater, Drinking Water, and Engineering. The data collected and analyzed directly informs engineering models, regulatory compliance, infrastructure investment decisions, and environmental protection efforts—making this an essential role in advancing the City’s mission to protect public health and the environment.

Classification Framework:
Environmental Compliance Analyst

What You'll Do

The following duties are a sample of major duties performed in this role and not intended to be an exhaustive list:

Conduct flow monitoring activities including field equipment maintenance, sensor replacement, and data validation
Collect water samples across drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, groundwater, and surface water systems
Calibrate and maintain analytical instruments and monitoring equipment to ensure accurate data collection
Perform stormwater and environmental sampling during qualifying weather or system events
Monitor and sample permitted industrial dischargers to ensure regulatory compliance
Analyze, interpret, and summarize environmental and operational data for reports and decision-making
Prepare technical reports, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and monitoring plans
Support biosolids, groundwater, and wastewater treatment facility monitoring programs
Troubleshoot mechanical and technical issues in field instrumentation and monitoring systems
Maintain compliance with safety protocols, including confined space entry, hazardous materials handling, and traffic control

Ideal Candidate

We’re looking for someone who is a self-starter, detail-oriented, and comfortable balancing multiple priorities in a dynamic environment. The ideal candidate enjoys hands-on, field-based work and can adapt to changing conditions while maintaining a high level of accuracy and safety. They bring a proactive approach to problem-solving and take initiative in maintaining and improving systems and processes.

Highly qualified candidates will have working knowledge of environmental monitoring practices, water and wastewater systems, and regulatory compliance requirements. They bring strong skills in data analysis, technical troubleshooting, and clear communication—both written and verbal. The ability to interpret data, identify anomalies, and connect findings to system performance is critical to success in this role.

Candidates who meet the listed minimum qualifications, including an equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered for an interview. Please ensure your application includes information about your education, relevant paid and unpaid work experience, and applicable licenses and certifications. Avoid referencing your resume in the job duties section of the application.

Minimum Qualifications

Education: Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, engineering, chemistry, biology, or a related field; AND
Experience: Relevant experience in environmental monitoring, water quality, wastewater/stormwater systems, or related technical field; OR
An equivalent combination of education and experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential duties of the job

Required Licenses & Certifications

Valid Oregon Driver’s License (or ability to obtain by date of hire)

Desired (but not required) Attributes

Experience with environmental sampling and laboratory procedures
Familiarity with EPA, DEQ, or other regulatory frameworks
Experience working with field instrumentation or monitoring equipment
Knowledge of data management, analysis tools, or reporting systems
Experience in municipal or public sector utilities

What To Know Before Applying

Application Deadline

Applications received by July 17
, 12:00 PM (noon) Pacific Time
will be included in an initial review and consideration for interview; however, the position will remain open until filled.

Application Requirements

To be considered for an interview, applicants must complete an online application including the following attachments:

Cover Letter
Resume

Veterans’ Preference

Applicants seeking Veterans’ Preference as a qualified veteran or disabled veteran must attach appropriate documentation to their application. For more information click here .

Equity Statement

The City of Bend remains committed to building a workforce that advances diversity and inclusion within our community and all we do. We recognize that not everyone starts from the same place, and that gender, race, ability, sexual orientation, and other identities face different barriers. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are dedicated to creating an inclusive, safe, and respectful workplace where employees can thrive without these barriers. A more extended version of the City of Bend’s Organizational Equity Statement is available upon request.

Benefits

The City of Bend offers an excellent competitive benefits package for Employees and Dependents for health and dental coverage, retirement benefits, and a robust paid leave program. Details are available on the benefits tab of the job posting.

Starting Compensation

Starting compensation is determined based on a pay equity analysis considering the candidate’s education, applicable work experience, and internal equity. Please include all relevant information on your application.

The City of Bend is committed to fostering, cultivating and preserving a culture of diversity and inclusion. At the City of Bend, we don't just accept differences; we value them. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and support the Americans with Disabilities Amendments Act (ADAAA) and the Oregon Equal Pay Act.

EKI Environment & Water, Inc. (EKI) is an employee-owned, full service, engineering and environmental sciences consulting firm serving private- and public-sector clients throughout the United States. If you are interested in improving water management strategies and practices, improving the environment, and advancing your career, then EKI is the place for you.

The Water Resources Project Manager position reports to the Team Leader (TL) and is responsible for project management and technical oversight of high-impact projects with California clients from initial project planning through implementation. Projects include Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) compliance and implementation, groundwater basin characterization, development of water budgets and water accounting frameworks, litigation support, water supply planning, and more.

Coordinate SGMA implementation for groundwater basins across multiple Groundwater Sustainability Agencies
Oversee hydrogeologic conceptual model development, water balances, numerical models, and projects and/or management actions deemed necessary by the client
Prepare well-written technical memorandums or reports and studies, including groundwater sustainability plans (GSPs), SGMA annual reports, and periodic evaluations of adopted GSPs
Point of Contact for client; coordinate and lead client meetings and related meetings and coordination with external parties
Plan, organize, and manage staff to deliver quality project work products on time and within budget
Prepare effective presentations that efficiently communicate complex technical concepts to a broad audience

Other duties as required

At least two (2) years of proven project management experience
Master's or PhD degree, and Professional Registration, or more than 12 years of demonstrated professional experience where Professional Registration is not available for degree, is desirable
Technical knowledge of SGMA, Groundwater Sustainability Plans, data management and visualization, ArcGIS, quantitative analysis (including numerical modeling), land subsidence, and technical writing

Department of Food \& Agriculture

### **Job Description and Duties**


**Per CCR 249\.3, this job control may be used to fill subsequent vacancies.**


Under the general direction of the Environmental Program Manager I, the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) (SES) is responsible for overseeing the operations of the Milk and Dairy Food Safety Branch Central Region Office in Fresno, California. The incumbent will be responsible for the supervision of Environmental Scientists that conduct environmental health inspections on dairy farms and milk processing plants, gather scientific data, research and investigate food safety hazards, test pasteurization equipment for proper operation and food safety controls, and provide analytical expertise and reports on specific food safety parameters on dairies, processing plants, haulers and other dairy food facilities, including those associated with possible illegal sales of substandard or unsafe dairy products to California consumers.  

  

  

As an employee of the California Department of Food \& Agriculture (CDFA), you are required to perform the “essential functions” of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. If you are interested in becoming part of a diverse and inclusive workforce where talent, experience, and expertise are valued, then CDFA is the place for you!!  

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. The CDFA does not participate in E\-Verify for employment authorization purposes.


You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


The duties of this position are primarily conducted indoors approximately 80% of the time. The incumbent has an office in the Central Regional Office located in Downtown Fresno. The office is furnished with all the necessary equipment for job performance and function.  

Incumbents must be able to establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted during the course of the work, work well under pressure, make appropriate decisions and recommendations, work independently to complete assignments and meet deadlines.  

When working outdoors the incumbent may be exposed to extremes in temperatures and high noise levels in a variety of environments ranging from individual dairy farm premises to complex, multi\-story processing plants complexes.  

Occasional travel (including nights and weekends) may be required for meetings, events, and field support as needed. A state issued vehicle may be assigned to drive on state business.  

The incumbent must follow CDFA, Division, and Branch employee health and safety policies.  

This position may/may not be eligible for telework. The amount of telework is at the discretion of the CDFA and based on the current telework policy. While CDFA supports telework where possible, in\-person attendance may be required based on operational needs. Employees are expected to be able to report to their worksite with minimal notification if an urgent need arises, as determined by the Department.

The Mission of the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) is to safeguard a resilient food system and promote an equitable marketplace, cultivating a California grown food supply that is globally recognized for innovation, quality, and sustainability.


The Milk and Dairy Food Safety Branch is responsible for ensuring that milk, dairy products, and products resembling milk products (PRMP’s) are safe, unadulterated, and properly labeled to safeguard public health. The Branch inspects dairy farms, bulk milk tanker trucks, and milk processing plants; issues permits and licenses to dairy farms and processing facilities; collects samples for regulatory testing to ensure compliance with food safety and quality standards; reviews product labels for conformance with regulations to avoid misleading information for consumers; completes in\-depth reviews and food safety assessments of complex equipment or novel processing methods, and evaluates and licenses technical food safety competencies of dairy industry workers. The Branch also responds to food safety incidents, and initiates product impounds and recalls as warranted. Review Environmental Monitoring data, trends, deviations, and excursions and support timely investigation, corrective action, and effectiveness activities as applicable

jobs.title: Manager, Environmental Compliance & Strategy
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Pattern Energy is a leading renewable energy company that develops, constructs, owns, and operates high-quality wind and solar generation, transmission, and energy storage facilities. Our mission is to transition the world to renewable energy through the sustainable development and responsible operation of facilities with respect for the environment, communities, and cultures where we have a presence.

Our approach begins and ends with establishing trust, accountability, and transparency. Our company values of creative spirit, pride of ownership, follow-through, and a team-first attitude drive us to pursue our mission every day. Our culture supports our values by fostering innovative and critical thinking and a deep belief in living up to our promises.

Pattern Energy operates in the United States and Canada, with offices in San Francisco, Houston, San Diego, New York and Toronto. Pattern Energy Group's corporate headquarters are in San Francisco. Pattern has a global portfolio of more than 35 power facilities and transmission assets, serving various customers that provide low-cost clean energy to millions of consumers.

Responsibilities

JOB PURPOSE

The Manager, Environmental Compliance & Strategy, EPC is responsible for ensuring environmental compliance and supporting strategic risk planning for Pattern’s projects during execution, with a primary focus on wind, transmission, and solar energy projects in the United States and Canada, and ancillary support for compliance efforts in other jurisdictions as needed.

This role leads and coordinates environmental construction permit compliance activities, supports environmental compliance programs and tools, and works closely with internal project teams, consultants, contractors, regulatory authorities, and local interest groups to ensure Pattern’s projects meet applicable environmental permit, regulatory, and internal compliance requirements.

To support ongoing Pattern projects, viable candidates may also be considered if they live near Pattern project locations in Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Louisiana, Montana, North Dakota, or New Mexico, as an optional work location arrangement.

Key Accountabilities

The key responsibilities will include as a minimum the following:

Lead environmental construction permit compliance activities in coordination with Pattern EPC group managers, engineering and construction managers, project construction contractors, and Pattern Environmental Development and Operations teams.
Manage and coordinate project environmental personnel, including environmental consultants, EPC and specialty contractors, regulatory authorities, and local interest groups as appropriate.
Conduct environmental compliance reviews, participate in monthly management meetings, complete site audits, and support compliance root-cause analysis investigations and reviews.
Assist in the development and implementation of Pattern environmental compliance programs, procedures, and project execution documents.
Create, maintain, and update project environmental compliance matrices during project execution.
Develop and deliver Environmental Awareness Training for EPC and contractor staff.
Coordinate with federal, state, provincial, and local environmental agency leads to resolve environmental concerns during construction.
Budget for and manage consultants providing project-level environmental support services, including construction environmental monitoring and wildlife mitigation strategies.
Represent Pattern in industry organizations and technical committees, supporting benchmarking, collaboration, and thought leadership across the renewable energy sector.

Qualifications

Experience/Qualifications/Education Required

Educational Experience

A bachelor’s degree in a science-oriented field such as Biology, Ecology, Environmental Sciences, Wildlife, or a related field is required. An advanced degree in Law, Biology, Environmental Sciences, Ecology, or a comparable discipline is preferred.

Required Work Experience

The following criteria will be used as a basis for Pattern to select a qualified applicant:

Seven or more years of experience in environmental, natural resources, or energy-related projects, preferably in renewable energy.
Experience with wind, transmission, and/or solar power permitting, environmental construction compliance, and environmental fieldwork.
Familiarity with federal, state, and provincial environmental regulations related to stormwater, hazardous materials, hazardous waste, air quality, wildlife, archaeology, environmental due diligence, and associated compliance programs.
Extensive experience with stormwater best management practices, including design, implementation, maintenance, and cost considerations.
Experience collaborating with cross-functional project teams and managing environmental consultants and contractors.

Additional Requirements

Must possess strengths in the following:

Strong time management, diplomacy, and specialized environmental compliance knowledge.
Ability to make informed recommendations regarding the interpretation and application of environmental permits, regulations, and laws in evolving regulatory environments.
Ability to analyze, organize, and interpret data from multiple sources and translate findings into clear written deliverables.
Strong professional communication skills, including the ability to influence best practices and change within projects and the broader organization.
Ability to multi-task, adapt quickly, work well under pressure, collaborate in large teams and one-on-one settings, and work independently with minimal supervision.
Willingness and ability to travel as needed, up to approximately 25%, depending on project needs.

Technical Skills

Computer skills – working knowledge of Windows-based business software applications, including Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint.

Environmental compliance – detailed knowledge of environmental regulatory frameworks, including wildlife, natural resources, stormwater, site restoration, spills, waste, audits, and project-specific permit or regulatory requirements for projects in the United States and/or Canada.

The expected starting pay range for this role is $103,000 - $138,000 USD. This range is an estimate and base pay may be above or below the ranges based on several factors including but not limited to location, work experience, certifications, and education. In addition to base pay, Pattern’s compensation program includes a bonus structure for full-time employees of all levels. We also provide a comprehensive benefits package which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life insurance, voluntary benefits, family care benefits, employee assistance program, paid time off and bonding leave, paid holidays, 401(k)/RRSP retirement savings plan with employer contribution, and employee referral bonuses.
